text:
Nora King: Noticing a recurring onboarding bug. New devs run `redwood login` which writes ~/.redwood/token, then start node sample app and immediately see 401s. The reason: node SDK only checks REDWOOD_API_KEY. Can we standardize?

Liam O'Connor: Saw the same in support chat. Python and CLI are forgiving; node is strict. First impression matters.

Hannah Yu: Quick proposal: single precedence order across SDKs/CLI: 1) REDWOOD_API_KEY (env) 2) REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN (env, service-scoped) 3) REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE (env path, default ~/.redwood/token) 4) OS keychain. Keep REDWOOD_ORG and REDWOOD_PROJECT purely for routing default.

Marco Silva: Agree with precedence. Small tweak: allow users to pass an explicit credentials object to SDK to override all sources. That helps test harnesses.

Nora King: Also: when SDK falls back to token file, it should log (info) "using credentials from ~/.redwood/token" and emit an analytics event only if telemetry enabled. That reduces guesswork for users and support.

Liam O'Connor: For rotation, suggestion: auth gateway returns 401 with header `x-rw-auth-status: expired` when token expired, or `x-rw-auth-status: invalid` otherwise. SDKs should: on expired -> try next source once, emit `auth:expired` event and surface friendly error hinting `redwood login`; on invalid -> fail fast.

Hannah Yu: Example node API shape I've sketched: 
```
const provider = new CredentialProvider({order: ['env','serviceEnv','file','keychain']})
const client = new Redwood({ credentials: provider, refreshOn401: true })
client.on('auth:expired', () => console.warn('token expired, run `redwood login`'))
```

Marco Silva: Tests: unit test provider precedence, integration test simulating gateway 401 headers. Also update samples to expose `whoami` helper: `redwood whoami` returns JSON with fields: org, project, credential_source. That should be callable by sample scripts to explain what they used.

Nora King: Can we avoid adding too many new env names? I like REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE rather than creating a new long var. But make defaults explicit in docs.

Liam O'Connor: +1. Also add a subtle UX: when env contains both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN, prefer service token only for service-scoped routes; otherwise env override wins. Document clearly.

Hannah Yu: I'll draft the spec and a short migration note for quickstarts: "If you used `redwood login`, samples will pick up CLI credentials; if you export REDWOOD_API_KEY, that takes precedence."

devx-bot: Created RDW-8345: "Credential precedence parity + whoami + auth status header" assigned to @Hannah Yu.

Marco Silva: I'll take node SDK work: implement CredentialProvider, add `credential_source` in client metadata, add refreshOn401 flow. Will open PR with tests and sample updates.

Nora King: We should also update the console login tooltip: "Use redwood login to persist a CLI token (used by samples) or set REDWOOD_API_KEY for processes." Small copy change reduces confusion.

Liam O'Connor: Acceptance checklist: spec doc, node provider + tests, sample whoami + startup logging, CLI whoami command, gateway header tweak. If all met, we should see fewer support tickets.

Hannah Yu: Will do python follow-up once node lands. Thanks team.

Marco Silva: PR incoming today.
